item.title: Music Fans React to Zakes Bantwini and Black Coffee’s Reunion After 15 Years - SlikourOnLife
item.description: South African music fans have taken to social media to react to the reunion of Black Coffee and Zakes Bantwini, who recently shared a stage together for the first time in what has been reported to be 15 years. The two artists, known for their contributions to the country’s house music scene, last collaborated on notable tracks such as “Juju” in 2011, following earlier work on projects including “Have Another One” and “Home Brewed.”

item.title: Danya Devs Steps Into Youth Development With CPC Stars Leadership Role - SlikourOnLife
item.description: Danya Devs is entering a powerful new phase—one that reaches far beyond music. With a recent announcement that signals growth, purpose, and a deeper connection to the next generation, he’s stepping into a role that could reshape how his influence is felt. This move hints at a story bigger than his own success, one rooted in building something lasting. Find out what this new chapter means and why it matters.

item.title: “Probably Number One of All Time,” Zingah Names Sjava Among His Top Five KZN MCs - SlikourOnLife
item.description: During a visit to the set of the “4PLAY” music video, Zingah shared insight into his top five KwaZulu-Natal MCs. “Not in any order because I’ve never thought of this,” he said, before naming Zakwe, Duncan, Shaun G, and Zuluboy. He then added, “ I’d have to put Sjava in there...probably number one of all time.”

item.title: Chase Bell And Lira Unveil Emotion-Driven New Single ‘Do Me’ - SlikourOnLife
item.description: Chase Bell has officially unveiled his latest single Do Me alongside South African icon Lira, but the story behind the release runs deeper than just music. From a personal journey to a cross-continental connection, this collaboration carries a meaning that goes beyond the surface. Tap in to discover what makes this release so significant.

item.title: LaCabra on Nasty C Sending Back ‘Shout Out To Me’ Verse in Just 30 Minutes - SlikourOnLife
item.description: LaCabra has revealed that Nasty C’s verse on “Shout Out To Me,” from his album Mr Bully, was completed in under an hour. “With Nasty, it took about 30 minutes, if I’m being honest,” he said. “I sent him about five songs one by one, and he kept saying I should send another one. Then I sent him ‘Shout Out To Me,’ and he went crazy.” He added that within 30 to 40 minutes, Nasty C had recorded and sent the verse back, marking a quick turnaround from selection to completion.
